bibliographic.title: A Federated Architecture for Sector-Led AI Governance: Lessons from India
bibliographic.venue: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
bibliographic.citation_apa: Agarwal, A., & Nene, M. J. (2026). A federated architecture for sector-led AI governance: Lessons from India. Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy. https://doi.org/10.1108/TG-09-2025-0310

methodology.method_family: conceptual framework application with illustrative case study
methodology.study_design: application of an established five-layer conceptual framework to the Indian context, validated through a detailed case study on AI incident management
methodology.sector: whole-of-government AI governance; cross-sectoral public policy in India
methodology.technology_context: general AI governance architecture and federated national AI incident management; no LLM or conversational system focus in provided text

eligibility.exclusion_reason: Out of scope for central or supporting evidence on conversational governance in LLM-based systems; addresses national sector-led AI governance architecture rather than conversational AI, chatbots, agents, RAG, guardrails, or related operational controls.
eligibility.decision_rationale: The manuscript clearly contributes institutional AI governance architecture, accountability, standards, and incident management for India's sector-led model, which aligns partially with regulated high-stakes governance themes. However, the provided text discusses AI generically, contains no LLM-specific content, and the only conversational match is metaphorical ('national conversation'), not conversational AI systems. It may inform macro-level governance context but not conversational LLM governance mechanisms.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter provided; boundary case between regulated AI governance and conversational LLM governance; Python metadata title extraction is corrupted.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal based only on author accepted manuscript front matter. Objective and high-level findings are clear; empirical rigor of the incident-management case study cannot be assessed from the excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: Internally coherent conceptual policy-architecture paper with stated case-study validation, but provided text is limited and relevance to conversational LLM governance in regulated deployments is weak.

coding.subtheme: Federated AI incident management and standards-based coordination

synthesis.main_claim: India's sector-led AI governance can be made coherent through a whole-of-government federated architecture, demonstrated via a national AI incident management design using common standards across sectors.
synthesis.contribution: Provides two actionable architectures—national governance role assignment and a federated incident-management model—that bridge policy principles and operational implementation, with claimed global transferability.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence on national/sectoral AI governance, accountability, standards, and incident management in regulated environments; not usable as central or supporting evidence for conversational LLM governance mechanisms.
